findings.title: Thread and cross-agent checkpoint isolation is based on client-supplied identifiers without per-user ownership checks
findings.detail: All registered graphs share one saver. Configurable state contains thread_id and user_id but no agent partition. Root backend checkpoint keys use thread_id/checkpoint_ns; application does not establish a separate agent namespace. history accepts only thread_id and selects DEFAULT_AGENT. Optional bearer secret authenticates possession of one shared secret, not thread ownership. Multi-chat UUID separation exists, but user/agent isolation is not enforced.

findings.title: SQLite/Mongo long-term store is volatile; registered graphs have no observed store consumer
findings.detail: SQLite checkpoints are file-backed, but initialize_store returns InMemoryStore for SQLite and Mongo. PostgreSQL uses AsyncPostgresStore. The only observed store read/write consumer is interrupt_agent birthdate with namespace(user_id), and that example is not registered. Therefore cross-thread personal memory is infrastructure/example capability, not demonstrated behavior of the active UFPI graphs.

findings.title: Checkpoint serializer omits excluded QueryResult audit fields
findings.detail: Synthetic default JsonPlusSerializer roundtrip loses excluded response_kind/generation_attempts/output_audit, restoring generated/1/None from clarification/0/present; public dump equal. Not a live service restart test.

findings.title: Persisted normative result is not returned by legacy history/message projection
findings.detail: AgenticState includes structured chunks, result, temporal intent, grounding and audits. Generation adds an AIMessage containing only result.answer. Legacy invoke and history project messages only, so retained structured normative references, temporal provenance and result audit are unavailable through those endpoints. ToolMessage projection keeps text/tool_call_id but not artifact or full tool metadata. Prior conversational text must not be treated as authoritative normative evidence.

findings.title: Service image omits normative core package required by registered agent
findings.detail: Service Dockerfile installs dependencies with --no-install-project and copies only agents/core/memory/schema/service/run_service. The registered chatbot_ufpi_agentic imports rag_baseline, which is not copied. Source-only inference: an image built solely from this Dockerfile lacks the package. Corpus/Chroma path provisioning is also absent; no container build executed.

findings.title: Two model/configuration paths coexist with different provider transports and selection semantics
findings.detail: Legacy core.settings selects an available provider/model and core.llm.get_model caches provider-specific LangChain wrappers. The normative core independently loads BaselineSettings and uses an httpx OpenRouterClient with its own generation, routing and embedding selectors. The agentic adapter lazily applies a hardcoded corpus profile, overriding corpus/index fields. No consolidation or model changes made. Effective local private environment values were not loaded or disclosed.

findings.title: Azure deployment map is validated but does not control model factory deployment
findings.detail: AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_MAP is required/validated in Settings, but get_model passes its enum model name directly as deployment_name and never reads the map. This is a confirmed ineffective configuration field; no credentials or provider calls inspected.

findings.title: Default request model differs from dynamically selected service default
findings.detail: UserInput.model has a fixed OpenAIModelName.GPT_4O_MINI default. Service passes user_input.model through configurable without substituting Settings.DEFAULT_MODEL. A request omitting model can therefore differ from advertised default; effects depend on selected agent, as normative graph uses its independent BaselineSettings client.

findings.title: Default development Compose does not force PostgreSQL and does not persist default SQLite file on a named volume
findings.detail: Development Compose starts PostgreSQL but agent_service only loads env_file and mounts privatecredentials; backend choice remains Settings/env-dependent. Production Compose explicitly defaults DATABASE_TYPE to PostgreSQL and provides postgres_data plus app_state; SQLITE_DB_PATH is placed in app_state there. SQLite restart durability requires same persistent file; container recreation on development defaults has no app_state mount.

findings.title: Relevant installed metadata matches locked versions and declared constraints, with Python execution-mode drift
findings.detail: Inspected relevant package metadata matches uv.lock and all directly declared relevant constraints; no incompatible dependency edge found within selected package set. pyproject and lock require >=3.11, audit process uses Python3.11, while both Dockerfiles pin3.12.3 and langgraph.json selects3.12. Existing .venv reports3.11 and .local/venv-agentic reports3.12. No Python3.12 execution/container/provider import validation performed; metadata matching is not functional compatibility proof.

backends.conversation_durability: File-backed checkpoint history; survives process restart when same database file remains available.
Remote PostgreSQL checkpoints with schema setup and connection pool.
Remote MongoDB checkpoint and pending-write collections.
backends.cross_thread_store_durability: process only; Mongo store not implemented

lifecycle.standalone_run_agent_persistence: No initialize_database/store call; compiled agent defaults may have no checkpointer; service supplies it only through lifespan.

identity.thread: Client-provided or random UUID per request; UUID continuity supports multiple chats.
identity.user: Client-provided or random UUID per request; not an authenticated principal. Streamlit stores/reuses identifier in session/query parameters.
identity.session: Streamlit st.session_state plus query parameters; no independent backend session ownership record found.
identity.agent: No explicit root agent checkpoint namespace established; common saver shared across graphs.
identity.global_memory: One global store/saver object per service lifespan; checkpoint keys partition threads; sole store user partitions by user_id.

serialization.effective_library_default: JsonPlusSerializer; msgpack typed encoding with Pydantic model_dump and module/class reconstruction; pickle fallback defaults false.
serialization.checkpoint_payload: Graph channel values and pending writes, including messages/tool results and custom state when supported by serializer.
serialization.restart_conditions: Same database identity/path, compatible state schema and importable class modules; durable database availability. Mongo/Postgres restart behavior not executed.
serialization.tool_results: ToolMessage channel objects are checkpointed; legacy message projection reduces them to content and tool_call_id, omitting artifact/full metadata.
serialization.custom_state: Structured agentic decision/chunks/audit/result/temporal state participates in checkpoint; QueryResult excluded audit fields are omitted by model_dump.

conversation_memory_vs_normative_provena.conversation_memory: Thread messages/checkpoint state and optional cross-thread personal data; prior assistant text is not a normative authority.
conversation_memory_vs_normative_provena.normative_provenance: Fresh retrieved chunks, canonical source/article metadata, explicit normative references, version filtering, temporal grounding and output audit. Chroma corpus persistence is separate from checkpoint database.
conversation_memory_vs_normative_provena.fresh_query_behavior: route_query clears chunks/result/temporal_grounding; retrieval obtains eligible corpus evidence for current question. Prior messages are retained, but only latest human message supplies current question.
conversation_memory_vs_normative_provena.exposure_gap: Legacy service messages/history do not expose structured result references/provenance.

obsolete_or_ambiguous.profile_override: Agentic adapter applies a fixed corpus profile and overrides CORPUS_PATH/CHROMA_COLLECTION/CORPUS_ID_PREFIX/CORPUS_NAME/CORPUS_SOURCES for that path.
obsolete_or_ambiguous.unknown: Effective secrets/local environment selections and deployment-time settings intentionally not loaded. Configured remote service behavior not exercised.

configuration.urls_and_secrets_policy: Only variable names/functions and source locations recorded. No environment values, private credential content, API keys, JWTs, passwords or full connection DSNs recorded.

dependencies.pythonpath_mode: code/src plus code/.venv/Lib/site-packages; metadata inspection only

secret_detection.method: Read-only heuristic scan of current tracked text files only; regex recognition of private keys, provider token shapes, JWTs, AWS IDs and literal credential DSNs. F-string/template connection builders excluded. No git history or untracked private env/credentials scanned.
secret_detection.limitation: Heuristic absence of matches does not prove absence of all secrets. No values retained or printed.

suggestions: Run core/test_settings.py and core/test_llm.py separately; factory tests may construct provider wrapper clients, so audit test constraints must be checked before execution.
Run client and service utility tests with isolated environment and mocks; service/conftest.py imports app and can initialize production graph imports.
Inspect service streaming/e2e fixtures before execution: some use in-memory checkpoint/fake static graphs; Docker e2e requires network/services and is outside this delegated audit.
Add or run an isolated temporary-SQLite roundtrip of ToolMessage plus representative custom state, without importing production agents or services, to verify process reopen persistence.
Perform isolated JsonPlusSerializer QueryResult roundtrip to confirm output_audit/generation_attempts/response_kind loss without network.
Verify two thread IDs isolation and deliberate same thread/different user or agent reuse with a purpose-built fake graph.
Postgres/Mongo restart, TTL and ownership scenarios are unverified here; no remote connections authorized in this delegated audit.
